stubs.angle: In a .proto message declaration such as `string name = 1;`, what does the `= 1` mean?
stubs.answerHinge: It is the field number that identifies the field in the binary wire format; it is not a default value, and the field name is not sent on the wire.

stubs.angle: How do Server-Sent Events differ from WebSockets in message direction, the underlying protocol and reconnection?
stubs.answerHinge: SSE is a one-way server-to-client stream of text events over an ordinary HTTP response (text/event-stream), and the browser EventSource reconnects automatically. WebSockets upgrade the connection to a full-duplex framed protocol with no built-in reconnection.

stubs.angle: Which kinds of RPC methods can a gRPC service declare in a .proto file?
stubs.answerHinge: gRPC defines exactly four kinds: unary, server streaming, client streaming and bidirectional streaming. Distractors such as fire-and-forget or server callbacks are not gRPC method kinds.

stubs.angle: Which changes to a .proto message keep existing gRPC clients and servers working?
stubs.answerHinge: Adding a field with a new number and removing a field while reserving its number are safe. Changing a field's number or its type to an incompatible one, or reusing a deleted number, breaks deserialization.

stubs.angle: In proto3, how can a gRPC service tell an int32 field explicitly set to 0 from a field that the client never set?
stubs.answerHinge: A plain proto3 scalar does not track presence, so 0 and unset look the same. Presence requires the `optional` keyword (a Has property is generated) or a wrapper type such as `google.protobuf.Int32Value`, which maps to `int?` in C#.

stubs.angle: A hand-written ASP.NET Core SSE endpoint sets text/event-stream and writes `data: ...\n` per update, but the browser EventSource never fires onmessage; find the line.
stubs.answerHinge: An SSE event is dispatched only when a blank line follows it, so every event must end with `\n\n`; writing a single newline leaves the event unfinished in the client buffer.

stubs.angle: A user is signed in on a phone and a laptop: which SignalR call reaches both devices, and how does SignalR know the user id?
stubs.answerHinge: `Clients.User(id)` sends to every connection of that user, while `Clients.Client` targets one connection id. By default the user id comes from the ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier claim through IUserIdProvider.

stubs.angle: Why does a client stop receiving group messages after a network blip and automatic reconnect, and where should group membership be restored?
stubs.answerHinge: Group membership is tied to a connection id and is not preserved when the connection reconnects, so the server must re-add the connection, for example in OnConnectedAsync based on the user's state.

stubs.angle: How should a BackgroundService or a controller push a message to SignalR clients?
stubs.answerHinge: Inject `IHubContext<THub>` (or the strongly typed `IHubContext<THub, T>`) and use its Clients and Groups; creating a hub instance manually does not work because hubs are created per invocation and have no connection context outside it.

stubs.angle: Why is creating a new GrpcChannel for every call a performance problem, and what should be reused instead?
stubs.answerHinge: A channel owns the HTTP/2 connections and is expensive to create, while generated clients are lightweight, so a channel should be created once and reused, or the gRPC client factory should manage it.

stubs.angle: A server-streaming gRPC method sends results of parallel lookups with `Task.WhenAll(items.Select(i => responseStream.WriteAsync(i)))` and fails intermittently; find the line.
stubs.answerHinge: IServerStreamWriter does not support concurrent writes: a WriteAsync must complete before the next starts, so parallel results must be serialized, for example through a Channel<T> read by one writing loop.

stubs.angle: Under load, gRPC call latency to a service grows while the server CPU stays low and many long-running streaming calls are open on one channel; how do you diagnose and fix it?
stubs.answerHinge: An HTTP/2 connection allows a limited number of concurrent streams (commonly 100), so extra calls on the channel queue on the client; `SocketsHttpHandler.EnableMultipleHttp2Connections` or separate channels for long-lived streams remove the queueing.

stubs.angle: Why does a connection-level (L4) load balancer spread gRPC traffic unevenly across server instances, and what are the alternatives?
stubs.answerHinge: gRPC multiplexes all calls over a long-lived HTTP/2 connection, so an L4 balancer pins all of a client's calls to one instance; balancing needs an L7 proxy that balances per call or client-side load balancing in GrpcChannel.

stubs.angle: Which statements about how errors travel in gRPC on .NET are true?
stubs.answerHinge: The gRPC status is sent in grpc-status trailers while the HTTP status is normally 200, the client sees an RpcException with a StatusCode, and an unhandled non-RpcException on the server becomes StatusCode.Unknown with the message hidden unless EnableDetailedErrors is on.

stubs.angle: What must a raw ASP.NET Core WebSocket receive loop handle correctly regarding message boundaries and closing the connection?
stubs.answerHinge: One message can span several ReceiveAsync calls, so the loop must accumulate until EndOfMessage is true, and a received Close message must be answered with CloseAsync (or CloseOutputAsync) to complete the close handshake.

stubs.angle: An SSE progress feed works locally, but in production behind a reverse proxy clients get events in large bursts or only when the stream ends; what do you check and change?
stubs.answerHinge: Something between the app and the client buffers the response, typically proxy response buffering or response compression, so the stream must be excluded from buffering and compression and flushed after each event.

stubs.angle: A team needs to change the meaning and type of a field in a .proto contract that four other teams consume, each deploying on its own schedule; how do you run the change?
stubs.answerHinge: Never change a field in place: add a new field or a new versioned package/service (for example v2) alongside the old one, give the contract one owner with automated breaking-change checks, and remove the old field only after consumers migrate, reserving its number.

stubs.angle: A product needs in-app notifications pushed to the browser; how does a tech lead choose between SignalR, plain Server-Sent Events and periodic polling?
stubs.answerHinge: The choice follows the traffic shape and operations cost: one-way low-volume updates fit SSE or polling with ordinary HTTP infrastructure, while two-way messaging, groups and transport fallback justify SignalR and its scale-out requirements.

stubs.angle: Which risks must a team plan for before switching a SignalR app to rolling deployments?
stubs.answerHinge: Connections on a stopping instance drop, so clients need automatic reconnect and state refresh, group membership must be restored after reconnect, and renaming or changing hub method signatures breaks clients still running the old version.

stubs.angle: Twenty gRPC services each log calls and map exceptions to status codes differently; which mechanism should the team standardise on?
stubs.answerHinge: A shared gRPC server Interceptor registered through AddGrpc options applies to every method in one place, unlike per-method code or general HTTP middleware that does not see typed messages and gRPC status.

stubs.angle: How do you architect push delivery to millions of concurrently connected clients without coupling business services to connection handling?
stubs.answerHinge: Separate a dedicated connection tier (for example Azure SignalR Service or a gateway layer) from business services, which publish events through a broker, so connections scale and redeploy independently and fan-out cost does not land on the services.

stubs.angle: Clients of a live pricing feed over gRPC streams and SSE miss updates during reconnects and redeployments, and partners demand no gaps; how do you redesign the feed?
stubs.answerHinge: Transports do not guarantee delivery across reconnects, so the feed needs per-stream sequence numbers, a resume position from the client (such as SSE Last-Event-ID) and a bounded replay buffer, falling back to snapshot plus deltas when the gap is too old.
